name: war1gus
title: War1gus
description: War1gus Stratagus PAX port; converted Warcraft I assets stay on SD.
about: Verified ESP32-P4 build of the War1gus Stratagus port. The native menus and first mission path have been exercised on hardware. Requires a complete data tree converted from your original Warcraft I files; game data is not included. Full-campaign, save-state and all-control coverage is not certified. Movie soundtracks are separate optional OGG companions beside media/menu.paxmenu.
changelog: 0.1.5: retry the MIDI audio worker with smaller internal stacks when the AIO cannot allocate 32 KiB; retain the PAPP2-safe Guichan cleanup.
controls: Mouse or touch: select units and use the game menus
Hold Menu 3 s: return to the launcher

extract.instructions: HOST COMPUTER REQUIRED: war1tool is not an ESP32-P4 program. On Linux, use your own Warcraft I PC ISO and a local Wargus/war1gus source checkout. Install CMake, a C++ compiler, cdrtools (isoinfo), FFmpeg/ffprobe, Python 3, and Pillow. Run: python3 ~/code/pax/pax-recipe/tools/prepare_war1gus_iso.py --iso /path/to/warcraft.iso --source /path/to/war1gus --output /path/to/new-war1gus-data --soundfont /path/to/your.sf2. This builds war1tool, extracts and converts the game assets, prepares the PAX movie pack, and renders the movie audio companions. Copy the generated tree contents to /sd/roms/war1gus/. For movie sound, keep media/hintro.ogv.ogg, media/ointro.ogv.ogg, media/cave.ogv.ogg, and media/title.ogv.ogg beside media/menu.paxmenu. The movie picture plays without those optional audio files. Omit --soundfont to skip MIDI music rendering; supplying one also requires FluidSynth. The recipe PAX prepares the SD folders and shows these instructions; it does not run war1tool. Game assets stay private and are not uploaded. The PAPP2 build has been exercised on the AIO through movie playback and clean exit.
